holidays.name: National Dress Up Your Pet Day
holidays.description: Today is the day to put your dog, cat, or other patient animal in a tiny outfit. Think wizard capes, hot dog costumes and cozy sweaters. Pets who put up with it have earned a treat.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, light-hearted observance. It is part of the wave of pet-themed days that spread through social media and pet-loving communities, and its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Costume safety matters. Outfits should never restrict a pet's breathing, movement or vision, and some pets are happiest with just a bandana.

holidays.name: National Hot Pastrami Sandwich Day
holidays.description: This is a salute to peppery, smoky, steamed pastrami piled high on rye, usually with mustard and a pickle on the side. It's a good excuse to visit your local deli.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday of unclear origin. It celebrates a deli classic that Romanian Jewish immigrants helped bring to New York City in the late 1800s.
holidays.funFact: Pastrami is traditionally made by brining beef, coating it in spices like black pepper and coriander, smoking it, and then steaming it until tender.

holidays.name: International Kite Day
holidays.description: People of all ages head outside to fly colorful kites and fill the winter sky. The day is especially joyful in India, where kite festivals light up the skies.
holidays.origin: The day is tied to Makar Sankranti, the Indian harvest festival marked on January 14. Kite flying is a beloved tradition of the festival, especially in Gujarat, where it grows into a large international kite festival.
holidays.funFact: Some kite flyers coat their strings with glass powder for friendly mid-air kite battles. The goal is to cut your rival's kite loose.
